resources.string: The same for the whole family: a change reaches every phone at once.
A pen cannot dial 2.35 u, so the dose is rounded.
The meal\'s part and the correction are added first, the total rounded once.
The rules come from children\'s clinics\' handouts (Nationwide Children\'s, Phoenix Children\'s, Children\'s of Alabama). Pick the one your doctor wrote.
After the point 0.1–0.4 goes down, 0.5–0.9 up.
After the point 0.0–0.2 down to whole, 0.3–0.7 to a half, 0.8–0.9 up to whole.
Like “to the nearest”, only exactly 0.5 goes down: 2.5 → 2, but 2.6 → 3.
To the nearest half, exactly in between (2.25 or 2.75) goes down.
Everything after the point is dropped. Less risk of a low, the sugar may run higher.
Down to a half or a whole. Less risk of a low, the sugar may run higher.
Anything after the point goes up to the next unit.
Up to a half or a whole.

Over a limit: a red card and a separate confirm every time. Over twice the dose limit: treated as a mistake, it cannot be planned. A typical child\'s meal is about 50 g; 150 g is the largest meal tested in insulin dose studies.
From how much on the glucometer, how much to add. Below the first row: no correction. Only the glucometer counts, not the sensor.
